a.text: Every hunter runs into a wolf before they go into the wastes.

The wolf says: Mulberry wood makes sturdy bows, and stones can be sharpened into deadly blades; but you must shed the clothes on you to survive, for it is the only thing that does not belong in the barrens.
So the hunter who kept his long coat on... was caught by tree roots protruding into the corner of the coat, ensnared by vines so tightly he could not move until he heard the beasts encircling him.

Another hunter covered himself head-to-toe in armor... was washed away by the river current when the water rushed into the tiny gaps between the metal plates, dragged down into the mud on the riverbed.
Only one hunter took the wolf's advice, and received a gift from it. The wolf tore off its own pelt, and placed it on the hunter.
The fur fit him so well, as if he was born with it. It helped the hunter survive countless dangers unscathed.
The pelt was so smooth and clean. When the hunter left the wilderness, not a speck of blood could be found on it.
And the hunter never took it off—

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Even the hunter's descendants had a custom of wearing clothing so fitting yet comfortable... and slowly, it evolved into the suit you commonly see on Siracusans today.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: ...Nonno, you've been telling me this story from when I was a baby, and I still don't get it. I've grown up and you're still telling it.

spans.text: ...Nonno, you've been telling me this story from when I was a baby, and I still don't get it. I've grown up and you're

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Luchino, I'm nearly done with these two suits. We just need to sew on these buttons.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: You accepted this order on your own accord, so we must be meticulous in our work, no matter who the client is.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Go fetch the buttons from the back. You won't miss them, they have the Saluzzo's emblem.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Shouldn't I first bring them to Signorina Lappland for a fitting, and then we adjust the clothes afterward? As you taught me—

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: It's fine. That Saluzzo signorina doesn't need it, I'll decide if they need any alterations.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: But she didn't request to skip the fitting...

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I know what's on your mind, boy.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Sometimes our clients request complicated designs, sometimes they don't even have a picture of it in their head, but it's not our place to probe too much.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Remember, Luchino: Tailor de Montano did not gain our reputation purely from our precision tailoring.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: People and materials are the same—know them before making any move.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Go get those buttons. It's time to finish this order.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Oh... okay.
Luchino looks at the two beautiful sets of attire. They are completely different to any suit his grandfather has ever made.
A magnum opus to be sure, worthy of the 'Made by de Montano' labels. He just wishes to be a part of that.
Luchino subconsciously pats his pocket. Inside are a few buttons he privately made himself, also engraved with the Saluzzo emblem.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: I'll get them at once, Nonno.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: ...*sigh*

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I kept you waiting outside for quite long, didn't I? Please come in.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: You can't delay Signor Antonio's commission any longer, Umberto.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: The old Don's about to arrive, if you start now you can still finish it in time before the Carnevale.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: Push back your other commissions and come with me to Venezia Trucking. We won't take too much of your time.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: My current commission is also one I can't disappoint.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Nonno! I heard someone come in!

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: Umberto, you don't actually have to make those measurements yourself.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: Wanna go meet a real somebody, ragazzo?

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Huh? A—A somebody? Nonno, I—

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Luchino, give me the buttons.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Y—Yes!

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Here.
The young tailor nervously looks at his nonno's face.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Not bad.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: But not good enough for these two outfits, Luchino.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: B—But I compared them so many times! They're practically the same!

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Once you sew enough buttons, you'll be able to tell if they'll fit or not just by touching them. Go fetch mine.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Here, here! All here!

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: I—I just wanted to help you out!

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: Umberto, I think you're being too hard on the kid, personally.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Keep practicing, Luchino.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Yes, practice. I'll be good and get back to it once I bring back your medicine!

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Signore, surely you can tell this boy is too reckless.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: ...You amuse me, Umberto.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Apologies, but my recent Carnevale commissions leave me no time at all to go with you.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I promise you, I'll personally go over to apologize once I'm done here.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Of course, I'll pay for any subsequent expenses as well.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: You really think Signor Antonio cares about all that? All I care about, is that I can enjoy the Carnevale in peace, Umberto—

spans.text: You really think Signor Antonio cares about all that? All
care about, is that I can enjoy the Carnevale in peace, Umberto—

steps.text: Umberto de Montano. Figured you'd be here.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: You shouldn't be here, Zaaro.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: You lost your Fang and this round, so you ought to return to the barrens and wait for the next round to begin.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Calm down, Caesar.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: I know you have the best odds of being the alpha of this round, but there's no way I can just sit and wait.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: I smell a strong human scent on you. Have you already picked up a new toy?

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: If you did, then why did you come find me? Were you hoping I console you, Zaaro?

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: I'm fed up with how you deceive and trick your little pup, Grandma.

spans.text: I'm fed up with how you deceive and trick your little pup,

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: I summoned you here to share an interesting secret—where the last unidentified Fang is hiding.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: You're out of the game, yet you still try to interfere?

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Outsiders make the most eager audience.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Caesar, the bloody stench beneath your merciful appearance and your thirst for victory... I've always been able to sniff them out despite your efforts.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Besides, I don't care if you're interested in my information or not. I'm merely relishing it.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Your pup has a keen sense of smell. A pity our unidentified Fang has spent decades cleaning the scent of wolf off himself.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Umberto de Montano. A pathetic tailor.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: Zaaro, I guarantee you that when this round ends, you'll savor the pain of our bite.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Caesar, your anger is delicious as ever.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Unfortunately, I'm not even the first wolf to challenge our rules.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: A Vulpo? You a tourist? Sorry, Tailor de Montano's all stuffed up with orders right now, so commissions are closed.

steps.name: Smiling Signora
steps.text: You're the boss here?

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: Who cares if I am or not—
He does not dare to finish his sentence.
Because he has just seen the blade in her hands.
Right. How long has it been since anyone in this city walked around freely with a weapon in their hand?
A smile remains on the woman's face, but he has a feeling: one more word from him and her blade will surely stab through his throat, even if they are in Nuova Volsinii right now.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: *cough* Signora, this man is an employee of the Venezia Trucking.

steps.name: Smiling Signora
steps.text: Trucking? The famiglia sure has changed a lot since I left.

spans.text: The famiglia sure has changed a lot since I left.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: (A Vulpo... the scar on her face... this suit, and that blade—)

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: (The homicidal lunatic that defected and left the famiglia... but six years ago, didn't she already...?)

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: You should go, signore. Please send Signor Antonio my regards. Of course, my prior promise to you remains true.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: Tch... You... I... cazzo.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: (Grazie, Umberto.)

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Signora Venezia, you don't seem to have changed much.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You know me?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Your photos were always on the newspapers. Dominated the headlines for a long time.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I thought you would have informed your family first about your return to Siracusa.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I left them many years ago—I came here looking for you.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Yet you're not here to kill me. There's a familiar scent on you.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Vargo?

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Yes. He found me in Higashi through his connections, and we made a deal.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Are you sure you want to have our conversation while you bask in the sun and roll around the red leaves?

steps.name: Slackerly Beast Aristocrat
steps.text: (Big yawn)

steps.name: Slackerly Beast Aristocrat
steps.text: How else?

steps.name: Slackerly Beast Aristocrat
steps.text: I wouldn't have bothered helping that wolf out if not for the tiny bit of friendship we have.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: So you want me to return to Siracusa... and act as a bodyguard for someone?

steps.name: Slackerly Beast Aristocrat
steps.text: To 'solve a problem'.

steps.name: Slackerly Beast Aristocrat
steps.text: Do that, and you'll know the truth you've been chasing after.

steps.name: Slackerly Beast Aristocrat
steps.text: Why you couldn't find the culprit who hurt your daughter despite all the heads you took, and who exactly that is.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Are you serious? You're not making up an excuse to chase me away from this place?

steps.name: Slackerly Beast Aristocrat
steps.text: Hah. Your choice to believe it or not.

steps.name: Slackerly Beast Aristocrat
steps.text: Other than him, I should be the only one in this entire shrine who doesn't hate you, Ingrid.

steps.name: Slackerly Beast Aristocrat
steps.text: You raid the place whenever you come in here just to see him, and that makes me quite happy. Life at the shrine would be so dull otherwise.

steps.name: Slackerly Beast Aristocrat
steps.text: To be honest, I kind of want to follow you back to Siracusa for a little walk.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You're talking about a deep swamp... Your stubbornness and hobby of rolling about in the grass won't like it there.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Tell him I'm going back.

steps.name: Slackerly Beast Aristocrat
steps.text: Not telling him yourself?

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: It's for Lisa, he'll understand.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: After I came back to Siracusa, I also met with the Signore dei Lupi. You, Umberto de Montano, I honestly could not have imagined he really chose someone like you if he hadn't stated your very name...

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: A humble tailor like myself?

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I don't know how Vargo described me to you, but we do subtly differ in our views on some matters.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You don't look so good, Umberto.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Vargo told me the wolves always choose humans with some sort of impressive talent, but your health is quite poor.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: That ragazzo who just left, he's your...

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Luchino is a bright boy, but he just can't accept the fact that time is unbeatable.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I'm old, Ingrid. Simple as that.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Is Vargo well?

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I can't tell with them... Did he not come to you?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: We haven't seen each other for many years, I thought he'd long abandoned me.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Maybe he just didn't want to taint you with his scent and risk putting you in danger. That's my guess.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: ...Is that so?

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: To be honest, I've no interest in finding out what happened between you and Vargo.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I'm just here to solve a problem for you.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: He told me how to distinguish the other Fangs. I was thinking, why not take the first move and give them hell instead?

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: What do you think?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: It seems you can't refuse the conditions he gave you.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: But this swamp is difficult to leave, once you make even just half a step into the mud.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Uh... I'll meet Signor Alberto soon. Should I explain the suit design in detail?

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: —I can't, Nonno will get mad if he finds out.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: But if Signor Alberto asks me about it, surely I can't refuse to answer.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Becoming acquaintances with the don of Famiglia Saluzzo could be good for us...

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: I might even manage to get better medicine for Nonno. Or maybe I could even bring him to Columbia to see even better doctors.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Huff. Stop spiraling, Luchino.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: The address from Signorina Lappland... it was this way, if I'm not wrong—

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Uh... A truck?

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Why is it so fast?! It'll hit the—

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Hey!!
Luchino hugs the intricate box containing the suits as he stands on the street corner, and witnesses the accident happen.
A truck fully loaded with goods suddenly crashes into a car that was just about to turn at the intersection.
Glass shards scatter all over, the vehicle frames wrecked out of shape. A tire pops out from the truck.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: ...H—Help... Help them out!

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Merda, everyone's gone to the main street for the show...

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Hey, just hold on in there! I'll get you out—

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Um, what are these... hidden inside the tires?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Here, Gambino! The car we had our sights on!

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: That was just a damn coffee break, what the... We're done for!

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: We were unlucky enough getting assigned the dirty work, with none of the credit...

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: And now something just had to happen to the goods under our eyes—

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Much worse than that, I'm afraid. Look at the car that got hit. Look familiar to you?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Why do you even care who the hell got hit—

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Wait. That's. Leontuzzo's...

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: I gotta say, what you said about going back to Lungmen wasn't so terrible after all.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Let's get outta here before the cops and boss find out. We'll slowly settle the accounts between us after we're back there.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: We toiled to get a sliver of hope here. There's no way we can just throw in the towel now, don't forget why we came here to Nuova Volsinii, why we joined Venezia Trucking!

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: No Signora Sicilia, no Grey Hall, and no restrictions from the other famiglie.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Who knows, we might even manage to make up a famiglia of our own, Gambino.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: See the kid across the street with the box? He's the only witness—maybe he caught a glimpse of the goods stashed inside the truck too?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: ...I got you. Up to us to decide if he saw anything. You're such a scumbag, Capone.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Just trying to keep myself alive, and leave a good impression on the boss at the same time.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Let's go. Take him, and tell them we got the sole witness with us.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: And the goods...?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: That's for the recipient to think about. Don't forget, the boss stressed again and again we're just cover.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: As for Leontuzzo... Hmph, hope he's fine.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Andiamo. We gotta get that kid before someone else does.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Uh, you are here to help?

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Over here, someone's still inside the car—

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Lights out.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: I'll carry him.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: The box he was carrying...

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Take it with us. Don't leave any clues behind.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: You sure no one saw us?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Obviously. The first thing I did here was to survey the surrounding area.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Go.
'CLOSED'.
The cafe is quiet, save for the occasional electrical 'buzzing' from the shop sign at the entrance.
'Closed for three days. Customers new and old, do vote for my daughter Ophelia at the show contest—A week of free coffee for everyone if she wins the right to light up the parade cars on Carnevale!'

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: A smell. It's strong.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: I know you ran in here.
Sparks fly when a passing arrow strikes the dagger in Projekt Red's hand, and the impact numbs her hand slightly.
Quick reflexes. No wonder I'm not done hunting yet!
But I've got you now—
Huh?

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: I caught you.

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: Ow! If you weren't a Fang, I wanted to invite you to the pack.

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: Too bad Agnese wouldn't agree.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: Grandma is waiting for me. I must hunt you... and then the last one.

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: Huh? Having second thoughts?

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: ...No. Not anymore. I don't want to let Kal'tsit down. Grandma even more.

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: Best not get too close to a hunter!
Lunacub turns around as she shoots an arrow, and quickly slams into a window, shattering it and escaping into the streets.

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: Don't move. I won't miss this time for sure.

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: I need to confirm one thing with you before I drag you back to Agnese—
I see Vargo was telling me the truth.
The wolf pack is restless.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I spent quite the effort to find you two.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Though the rest will be simple to do.

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: You have a smell that Agnese hates, but you're not a Fang.

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: You know her, Projekt Red? Just show yourself, I won't shoot on sight.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: But her blade. Sharper than mine.

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: ...For real?

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: There's no telling who'll win like this.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: I will reach her first.
The red figure dashes towards Ingrid, and Lunacub quickly turns to aim at the blade-wielding Vulpo.

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: Not before my arrow does.

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: Three shots, and I'll have her cornered.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: Behind you.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Trying to distract me? Tsk.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I've handled tougher fights in Siracusa with many more people on the other end.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: But I'm always the last one standing. No exceptions.
Three arrows lodge into her sword sheath.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Don't treat humans like beasts. Your hunting skills won't work on me.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You can certainly continue to try. Same goes for you, 'Projekt Red'.

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: This is not over yet.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: My blade... not sharp enough...

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Come.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You can't hide from me forever. I won't wait any longer for Vargo's answers.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Are the police here actually working? I should go.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: The accident, the Fangs, and the Famiglia Venezia's shadow...

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I see Siracusa is welcoming me back with even bigger surprises.
